cards.text: Paul, called to be an apostle, is writing to all in Rome who are loved by God (Romans 1:1, 7). He has just written, 'What a wretched man I am! Who will rescue me from this body of death?' (Romans 7:24) Now he says, 'Therefore, there is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.'

cards.question: Paul gives the reason those in Christ Jesus aren't condemned. What did the law of the Spirit of life do for them?

answers.text: Set them free from the law of sin and death
Made them strong enough to obey every rule
Gave them a list of new rules to keep

cards.text: Paul says there's something the law was powerless to do, because it was weakened by the flesh. Picture a perfect stamper pressed into runny dough: great stamp, NOTHING holds.

cards.question: So God did what the law was powerless to do. How did He do it?

answers.text: He sent His own Son as an offering for sin
He gave His people a stricter law to follow
He sent His prophets with one more warning

cards.text: And Paul says how God sent His Son: in the likeness of sinful man.

cards.question: True or false: by sending His Son as an offering for sin, God condemned sin in the flesh.
Paul says God condemned sin in the flesh for a reason. What was it for?

answers.text: So the law's righteous standard is fulfilled in us
So the law could be set aside for good
So people would try harder to keep the law

cards.text: And Paul says that 'us' is those who do not walk according to the flesh but according to the Spirit. Flesh and Spirit, friend: keep your eye on those two.

Paul says those who live according to the flesh set their minds on the things of the flesh, and those who live according to the Spirit set their minds on the things of the Spirit. Me? My mind's been set on chocolate chips since day one, and my apron can PROVE it.

cards.question: Paul says the mind of the flesh is death, but the mind of the Spirit is ___ and peace.
Why does Paul say the mind of the flesh is death?

answers.text: Because it is hostile to God
Because it is too weak to try
Because it never hears God's law

cards.question: Paul says the mind of the flesh does not submit to God's law, nor can it do so. True or false: he says those controlled by the flesh can still please God.

cards.text: Then Paul turns to his readers: 'You, however, are controlled not by the flesh, but by the Spirit, if the Spirit of God lives in you.' Somebody just got some GOOD news.

cards.question: Paul says anyone who does not have the Spirit of Christ does not ___ to Christ.

cards.text: And Paul says if Christ is in you, your body is dead because of sin, yet your spirit is alive because of righteousness. Then he says one more thing about the Spirit who lives in you.

cards.question: True or false: Paul tells his readers in Rome that if the Spirit of the One who raised Jesus from the dead lives in them, He will also give life to their mortal bodies.

cards.text: So Paul tells the brothers they have an obligation, but it's not to the flesh, to live according to it. The flesh keeps mailing you bills, friend, and Paul says you don't owe it a THING.

cards.question: Paul says if you live according to the flesh, you will die. But if by the Spirit you put to death the deeds of the body, you will ___.

cards.text: Then Paul says all who are led by the Spirit of God are sons of God. I went from the back of a junk drawer to a gold base, and even I'm saying THAT is a bigger upgrade.

cards.question: Paul tells his readers they did not receive a spirit of slavery that returns them to fear. What does he say they received instead?

answers.text: The Spirit of adoption to sonship
A spirit of service under the law
A spirit of courage for the battle

cards.text: Paul says that by that Spirit we cry, 'Abba! Father!' Friend, that's not a servant knocking at the back door; that's family walking right in.

cards.question: Paul says someone testifies with our spirit that we are God's children. Who is it?
If we are God's children, what does Paul say that makes us?

cards.text: Heirs of God, and co-heirs with Christ. But Paul adds a condition: we share in what Christ went through, so that we may also be glorified with Him.

cards.question: Christ was sent as an offering for sin. What does Paul say we must do with Christ, so that we may also be glorified with Him?
